concept.name: Backtest engine
concept.definition: Software that coordinates historical data, the simulation clock, strategy callbacks, order state, portfolio accounting, and performance output.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Load dated data, enforce a time frontier, dispatch events or bars, call strategy logic, pass orders to reality models, and persist results.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: The engine advances to 10:01, invokes the algorithm, sends its order to a fill model, and books the returned execution.
